title: Sean McVay at his presser today on the prospect that the Rams' travel plan to Australia will be criticized if they lose to the 49ers: “It will be circumstantial based on what happens. What I think is the most important thing is we make decisions that we feel like are with the players’ best interests. And that’ll guide every approach. I understand the narratives. Hey, when we do good, it’s nice things. And when we do bad, you’re criticizing me in your column…. So I get it. I understand. I think that’s just part of the nature. But what you have to do is be able to separate the actual result from what is actually sound in terms of your process. I’m comfortable with that. That’s the world that we live in. And my job is to make sure that we’re making good decisions with the best thing in mind for those players…. That’s kind of the price of doing business.”

title: Some early takeaways from Melbourne roughly 24 hours in: - everything I’ve heard about this being a sports mad place is true. Fans everywhere in their respective gear. Everyone decked out for AFL playoffs last night and have been asked about the NFL game a handful of times already. - the coffee hype is real. Three different spots, three excellent cups. (Shoutout Dukes, Palace and Market Lane, also accepting recs from those in the know). - was told one of the reasons the NFL opted for Melbourne is the walkability. Absolutely true again. Other than airport to hotel haven’t been in a car at all. - only disappointment so far: walked past a theatre and saw “Dracula” advertised. Sadly, on further inspection, it was a ballet and not the long awaited Dracula musical.
summary:
Some early takeaways from Melbourne roughly 24 hours in:

- everything I’ve heard about this being a sports mad place is true. Fans everywhere in their respective gear. Everyone decked out for AFL playoffs last night and have been asked about the NFL game a handful of times already. 

- the coffee hype is real. Three different spots, three excellent cups. (Shoutout Dukes, Palace and Market Lane, also accepting recs from those in the know).

title: Thought about this quote from Michael Wilson a few times today. As a father and a son, it hit home. As parents, we sacrifice to make our kids' lives better. Our stories don't start with us, as Wilson's didn't start with the Senior Bowl. And I think I speak for every parent when I say we all hope our kids appreciate what we do for them like Wilson appreciates what his parents did for him. "I think it starts 50 years before the Senior Bowl," Wilson said. "My dad came from Montego Bay, Jamaica, grew up with a schizophrenic mom, came here when he was 18, was a construction worker for 35 years. He probably won't want me to say this, but he never made over $100,000 in his entire life, and my mom was born and raised in Wellington, New Zealand, came here in her mid-20s to pursue a nursing career. So, I think it starts at their story, right? Two immigrants came here. My mom, still to this day, doesn't know much about football. To be honest, she really doesn't like me playing football still. She's a nervous wreck during the season. And, so, this is a big win for the entire Wilson family and starting back from their story. I don't think if my dad could go back to my age at 26, he would [think he would] have a son playing in the NFL and same thing. I don't think my mom knew what American football was when she was 25, 26. So this is a big win for them and for their story more so honestly than mine because without them, I wouldn't have been able to achieve what I have."

title: Have see some media members question the overall ceiling of the Chargers roster compared to other potential contenders so I went and looked at the last 20 Super Bowl participants and how many Pro Bowlers and 1st team All Pros each had. Generally speaking you’re trying to get to 4 or 5 Pro Bowlers and 1 or 2 first team All Pros to be on that level. 4 teams made the SB with 3 Pro Bowlers or less: 2025 Patriots, 2021 Bengals, 2020 Bucs, and 2018 Patriots. 5 teams made the SB without any first team All Pro players: 2025 Patriots, 2021 Bengals, 2020 Bucs, 2019 Chiefs, and 2016 Patriots. Obviously health dependent but I think the Chargers could easily clear the general threshold with this year’s roster. That’s not where I have questions about this team, personally.

title: Brian Schottenheimer on Joe Milton: “When he informed me he was coming back, I was elated. This is a guy that’s worked his butt off to be where he is and to develop the way he has developed. And the talent is so rare. I think when you’re waived — I’ve been fired many times — you’re in shock a little bit. And then I think you kind of step back and you’re like, ‘OK, didn’t expect this, didn’t see this coming.’ But the more you think about it, you start figuring out the positives and negatives of the situation. “And for him to be able to stay here with the relationships that he’s built, understanding our system, understanding the locker room and other coaches, we were thrilled to get him back and he’s going to continue to get better. And that’s part of it. He got some reps (Thursday) along with Sam (Howell) and Dak (Prescott) and all those guys. I’m thrilled he’s back.” Schottenheimer said he was surprised Milton didn’t get signed by another team. “Totally. But I think you look around the landscape of the league, I mean, some teams are still holding four (quarterbacks). And so the quarterback rosters and quarterback rooms around the league are pretty crowded right now, but he certainly is talented enough to be claimed. But it’s our good fortune that he wasn’t.”
